In air the ionising power which is seen in the chamber at the focus is

$P_{abs}=I\,W/e$ , $W/e\simeq 33.97\;{\rm V}$

$P_{abs}=2.0\times10^{-12}\times33.97\simeq6.8\times10^{-11}\ {\rm W}$

in the air which is instantaneously in the $w_{f}\times h_{f}$ spot.
With

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}
      =0.030\,{\rm cm}\times0.60\,{\rm cm}=1.8\times10^{-2}\ {\rm cm^{2}}$

$V_{f}=A_{f}L=1.8\times10^{-2}\times15.1=2.72\times10^{-1}\ {\rm cm^{3}}$

$m_{a}=\rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}\times0.272\simeq
3.5\times10^{-4}\ {\rm g}=3.5\times10^{-7}\ {\rm kg}$

is the air mass which sees the 2.0pA at any instant.  On axis

$\dot K_{a}=P_{abs}/m_{a}=I\,W/e/m_{a}
      \simeq6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}
      \simeq1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}
      \simeq0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$

in air and with $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}=0.328\;
{\rm cm^{2}g^{-1}}$ at 33 keV

$\dot K_{t}\simeq\dot K_{a}\simeq1.9\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$

is the free-in-air tissue kerma rate in the $0.30\times6\;{\rm mm^{2}}$
micro-beam. The $\mu_{en}/\rho$ cancels in the $I\to K$ conversion and
is used only to justify $\dot K_{t}\simeq\dot K_{a}$.

A material point stays in the stationary $w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}$ slit for
the geometrical dwell quoted for the scan

$t_{d}=w_{f}/v_{s}\simeq0.02\ {\rm s}$ ,

so that the kerma acquired in one mono-energetic transit of one
resolution element is

$K_{1}=\dot K_{t}t_{d}\simeq1.93\times10^{-4}\times2.0\times10^{-2}
     \simeq3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$

per 33 keV dwell, i.e. $0.19\;{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times20\;{\rm ms}$,
in air and, to $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\approx(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}$, in soft
tissue.  This is the conventional $\sim4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per projection
synchrotron Laue micro-beam surface kerma.  In the usual $N_{E}=2$
material-decomposition implementation

$K_{DE}\simeq2K_{1}\simeq7\!-\!8\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq7\!-\!8\;
\mu{\rm Gy}\approx0.008\ {\rm mGy}$

per rastered surface element, $ 3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per energy, is the
dose actually received by a point during a standard dual-energy
multiple-energy acquisition.

The $50\;{\rm mm}$ horizontal illumination of the bent Laue crystal is
demagnified to $w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}$ at the focus,

$N_{E}\simeq W_{c}/w_{f}=50.0/0.30\simeq1.67\times10^{2},$

essentially independent energy positions in the Laue fan.  Summed over
the whole $W_{c}\times h=50\,{\rm mm}\times6\,{\rm mm}$ monochromator
field the peak kerma which can be built up on a point sampled through
the complete energy band is

$K_{M}\simeq N_{E}K_{1}\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}
      \simeq6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy},$

$\simeq0.64\;{\rm mGy}$ on the nominal numbers, i.e. $N_{E}$ times the
$3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-energy $20\;{\rm ms}$ dwell.  The
$3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}$ per 20 ms mono-energetic dwell,
$\approx7\!-\!8\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}$ dual-energy, is the per-energy
per-resolution-element peak surface kerma normally quoted for the
system; the $N_{E}K_{1}\sim 6\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}$ $\approx0.6\ {\rm
mGy}$ value is the $W_{c}/w_{f}$ integrated cumulative surface exposure
over the full $50\;{\rm mm}$ Laue fan, the sub-milligray cumulative
surface dose normally quoted for a bent-crystal multiple-energy scan.
The field-averaged mean over the 50 mm field is
$K_{av}=K_{1}w_{f}/W_{c}\sim2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}\ {\rm Gy}$ per
projection, $\sim70\!-\!80\;{\rm nGy}$ mean per energy.  The $10\times$
low values in the thread are the $A_{f}=0.18\;{\rm cm^{2}}$,
$0.30\;{\rm cm}$ instead of $0.030\;{\rm cm}$, mm$\to$cm conversion slip. ∎

3.text:
The power which is actually put into the air which is instantaneously in
the $w_{f}\times h_{f}$ focus is the conventional ionisation balance

$\dot E_{a}=I\,W/e$, $W/e\simeq33.97\,{\rm V}$

$\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}\times33.97\simeq6.8\times10^{-11}\ {\rm W}$ .

At the focus

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}
     =0.030\,{\rm cm}\times0.60\,{\rm cm}=1.8\times10^{-2}\ {\rm cm^{2}}$

$V_{f}=A_{f}L=1.8\times10^{-2}\times15.1=2.72\times10^{-1}\ {\rm cm^{3}}$

$m_{a}=\rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}\times0.272\simeq3.5\times10^{-4}
{\rm g}=3.5\times10^{-7}\ {\rm kg}$

is the air mass which sees the 2.0 pA at any instant, so that the on
axis air kerma rate in the $0.30\times6\ {\rm mm^{2}}$ micro-beam is

$\dot K_{a}=I\,W/e/m_{a}\simeq6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}
\simeq1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}\simeq0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$

in air.  With $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}=0.328\ {\rm
cm^{2}g^{-1}}$ at 33 keV

$\dot K_{t}\simeq\dot K_{a}\simeq1.9\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$

is the free-in-air tissue kerma rate in the $0.30\times6\ {\rm mm^{2}}$
focus, the $\mu_{en}/\rho$ cancelling in the $I\rightarrow K$ conversion.

A surface element stays in the stationary $w_{f}=0.30\ {\rm mm}$ slit for
the geometrical dwell quoted for the scan

$t_{d}=w_{f}/v_{s}\simeq0.02\ {\rm s}$ ,

so that the kerma accumulated in one mono-energetic transit of a
resolution element through the stationary focus is

$K_{1}= \dot K_{t}t_{d}\simeq1.93\times10^{-4}\times2.0\times10^{-2}
\simeq3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$

per 33 keV, $0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times20\ {\rm ms}$, free-in-air
$\approx$ soft tissue surface kerma.  This is the conventional
$\sim4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per projection synchrotron Laue micro-beam number.
For the usual material-decomposition implementation

$K_{DE}\simeq N_{E}K_{1}$ with the conventional $N_{E}=2$,

$K_{DE}\simeq2\times3.9\times10^{-6}\simeq7\!-\!8\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}
\simeq7\!-\!8\;\mu{\rm Gy}\approx0.008\ {\rm mGy}$

per rastered surface element, $\approx4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per energy, the
normally quoted per-point multiple-energy surface dose.

The $50\ {\rm mm}$ horizontal illumination of the bent Laue crystal is
demagnified to $w_{f}=0.30\ {\rm mm}$ at the focus.  The number of
essentially independent energy / beam positions contained in the Laue
fan is

$N_{E}\simeq W_{c}/w_{f}=50.0/0.30\simeq1.67\times10^{2}$ ,

so that the kerma which can be summed over the whole $W_{c}\times h=
50\ {\rm mm}\times6\ {\rm mm}$ monochromator field for a point which is
sampled through the complete energy band is

$K_{M}\simeq N_{E}K_{1}\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}
      \simeq6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$

per complete $50\ {\rm mm}\times6\ {\rm mm}$ multiple-energy scan,
$\approx0.64\ {\rm mGy}$ on the nominal numbers, i.e. $N_{E}$ times the
$3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-energy $20\ {\rm ms}$ dwell.  The mean kerma
averaged over the 50 mm field is $K_{av}=K_{1}w_{f}/W_{c}\sim2\!-\!3
\times10^{-8}\ {\rm Gy}$ per projection, $\sim70\!-\!80\ {\rm nGy}$ mean
per energy.

In particular $ \dot K_{t}\approx1.9\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$,
$K_{1}\approx3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per 20 ms mono-energetic dwell and
$K_{DE}\approx7\!-\!8\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ for the conventional dual-energy
pair are the per-energy / per-point surface doses.  The
$W_{c}/w_{f}\approx167$-fold field-integrated cumulative surface kerma
normally quoted for the bent-crystal multiple-energy system is the
$\sim6\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\sim0.6\ {\rm mGy}$ value above, $ \sim
0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$ peak reduced to $\sim4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per
energy $20\ {\rm ms}$ dwell.  The $10\times$ low $3.8\times10^{-7}\ {\rm Gy}$
estimates are the $A_{f}=0.18\ {\rm cm^{2}}$ mm$\to$cm slip. ∎

12.text:
The ionisation reading is the power which is put into the air which is
instantaneously in the $w_{f}\times h_{f}$ focus

$\dot E_{a}=I\,W/e$, $W/e\simeq33.97\;{\rm V}$ 

$\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}\times33.97\simeq6.8\times10^{-11}\ {\rm W}$ .

At the focus

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}
     =0.030\,{\rm cm}\times0.60\,{\rm cm}=1.8\times10^{-2}\ {\rm cm^{2}}$

$V_{f}=A_{f}L=1.8\times10^{-2}\times15.1=2.72\times10^{-1}\ {\rm cm^{3}}$

$m_{a}=\rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}\times0.272\simeq3.5\times10^{-4}\ {\rm g}
     =3.5\times10^{-7}\ {\rm kg}$

is the air mass which sees the 2.0 pA at any instant.  Hence on axis

$\dot K_{a}= \dot E_{a}/m_{a}=I\,W/e/m_{a}\simeq
6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}\simeq1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}
\simeq0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$

in air.  With $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}=0.328\ {\rm cm^{2}g^{-1}}$
at 33 keV

$\dot K_{t}\simeq\dot K_{a}\simeq1.9\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$

is the free-in-air tissue kerma rate in the $0.30\times6\,{\rm mm^{2}}$
micro-beam.  The $\mu_{en}/\rho$ cancels in the $I\to K$ conversion.

A material point stays in the stationary $w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}$ slit for the
geometrical dwell

$t_{d}=w_{f}/v_{s}\simeq0.02\ {\rm s}$ ,

so that the kerma accumulated in one mono-energetic transit of one
resolution element through the stationary focus is

$K_{1}= \dot K_{t}t_{d}\simeq1.93\times10^{-4}\times2.0\times10^{-2}
      \simeq3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\approx3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$

per 33 keV exposure, i.e. $0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times20\;{\rm ms}$,
essentially the same in air and in soft tissue at 33 keV.  This is the
conventional $\sim4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per projection synchrotron Laue
micro-beam surface kerma.

For the conventional two energy material decomposition which is the
usual multiple-energy implementation

$K_{DE}\simeq N_{E}K_{1},\qquad N_{E}=2$

$K_{DE}\simeq2K_{1}\approx7\!-\!8\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\approx7\!-\!8\;\mu{\rm Gy}
\approx0.008\ {\rm mGy}$ per rastered surface element, $K_{1}\approx3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$
per energy being the per-energy component.  The $1.9\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$
peak rate is the $0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$ rate at the focus reduced to
$\sim4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ by the 20 ms geometrical dwell.

The $50\,{\rm mm}$ horizontal illumination of the bent Laue crystal is
demagnified to $w_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}$ at the focus,

$N_{f}\simeq W_{c}/w_{f}\simeq50.0/0.30\simeq1.67\times10^{2}$,

essentially independent Laue energy positions in the fan.  Summed over
the whole $W_{c}\times h=50\,{\rm mm}\times6\,{\rm mm}$ monochromator
field the peak kerma which can be built up on a point which is sampled
through the complete energy band is

$K_{M}\simeq N_{f}K_{1}\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}
      \simeq6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$,

$\simeq0.64\ {\rm mGy}$ with the nominal numbers, i.e. $N_{f}$ times the
$3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-energy 20 ms dwell.  The field averaged mean over
the 50 mm line is $K_{av}=K_{1}w_{f}/W_{c}\sim2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}\ {\rm Gy}$
per projection.  The $3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per energy, $\approx7\!-\!8\;\mu{\rm Gy}$
dual-energy, is the normally quoted per-projection, per-resolution-
element surface dose; the $\sim0.6\ {\rm mGy}$ value is the $W_{c}/w_{f}$
integrated cumulative exposure over the full Laue fan.  The $10\times$
low $3.8\times10^{-7}\ {\rm Gy}$ estimates are the $A_{f}=0.18\,{\rm cm^{2}}$
i.e. $0.30\,{\rm cm}$ instead of $0.030\,{\rm cm}$ mm$\to$cm slip. ∎

18.text:
The ionisation rate is the absorbed power in the air which is
instantaneously in the $w_{f}\times h_{f}$ focus

$$\dot E_{a}=I\,W/e\qquad W/e\simeq33.97\;{\rm V}$$

$$\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}\times33.97\simeq6.8\times10^{-11}\ {\rm
W}$$

in the air that is in the beam at any instant.

$w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}=0.030\;{\rm cm}$,$\;h_{f}=6.0\;{\rm mm}=0.60\;{\rm
cm}$

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.030\times0.60=1.8\times10^{-2}\ {\rm cm^{2}}$

$V_{f}=A_{f}L=1.8\times10^{-2}\times15.1=2.72\times10^{-1}\ {\rm cm^{3}}$

$m_{a}=\rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}\times0.272\simeq3.5\times10^{-4}\ {\rm g}
=3.5\times10^{-7}\ {\rm kg}$

is the mass which sees the 2.0 pA  current at any instant.  Hence on
axis

$\dot K_{a}= \dot E_{a}/m_{a}=I\,W/e/m_{a}\simeq
6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}\simeq1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm
Gy\,s^{-1}}\simeq0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$

in air at the $0.30\times6\;{\rm mm^{2}}$ focus.  With
$(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}=0.328\;{\rm cm^{2}g^{-1}}$
at 33 keV

$\dot K_{t}\simeq\dot K_{a}\simeq1.9\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$

is the free-in-air, $\simeq$ soft-tissue kerma rate in the
micro-beam.  The $\mu_{en}/\rho$ cancels in the $I\to K$ conversion.

A surface element stays in the stationary $w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}$ slit
for the geometrical dwell quoted for the scan

$t_{d}=w_{f}/v_{s}\simeq0.02\;{\rm s}$ .

The kerma acquired in one mono-energetic transit of a resolution
element through the stationary focus is therefore

$K_{1}=\dot K_{t}t_{d}\simeq1.93\times10^{-4}\times2.0\times10^{-2}
\simeq3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\approx3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$

per 33 keV dwell, i.e. $0.19\;{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times20\;{\rm ms}$,
essentially the same in air and in soft tissue.  This is the
conventional $\sim4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-projection Laue micro-beam
surface kerma.

For the conventional two-energy material decomposition

$K_{DE}\simeq2K_{1}\simeq7\!-\!8\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq7\!-\!8\;
\mu{\rm Gy}\approx0.008\ {\rm mGy}$

per rastered surface element, $K_{1}\simeq3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per energy,
the normally quoted per-point, per-energy synchrotron surface dose.

The $50\;{\rm mm}$ horizontal illumination of the bent Laue crystal is
demagnified to $w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}$ at the focus,

$N_{E}\simeq W_{c}/w_{f}=50.0/0.30\simeq1.67\times10^{2}$

essentially independent energy positions in the Laue fan.  Summed
over the whole $W_{c}\times h=50\,{\rm mm}\times6\,{\rm mm}$
monochromator illumination the peak kerma which can be built up on a
point which is sampled through the complete energy band, i.e. the
field-integrated cumulative exposure delivered by the multiple-energy
system, is

$K_{M}\simeq N_{E}K_{1}\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\
{\rm Gy}\simeq6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$,

$\simeq0.64\ {\rm mGy}$ with the nominal numbers, $N_{E}$ times the
$3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-energy 20 ms dwell.  The field averaged mean
over the 50 mm line is $K_{av}=K_{1}w_{f}/W_{c}\sim2\!-\!3\times
10^{-8}\ {\rm Gy}$ per projection, $\sim70\!-\!80\;{\rm nGy}$ mean per
energy.

Hence the $0.19\;{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$ peak rate is reduced to
$\approx3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per mono-energetic 20 ms dwell and $\approx
7\!-\!8\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ for the usual $N_{E}=2$ dual-energy acquisition
per resolution element, the $ \sim0.6\;{\rm mGy}$ $W_{c}/w_{f}$ value
being the cumulative surface exposure integrated over the full
$50\,{\rm mm}\times6\,{\rm mm}$ Laue fan that defines the multiple-
energy imaging field.  The $10\times$ $A_{f}=0.18\;{\rm cm^{2}}$
estimates are the mm$\to$cm conversion slip $0.30\;{\rm mm}=0.030\;{\rm cm}$,
$A_{f}=1.8\times10^{-2}\;{\rm cm^{2}}$ used above. ∎

demagnified to $w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}$ at the focus

$N_{s}\simeq W_{c}/w_{f}=50.0/0.30\simeq1.67\times10^{2}$

essentially independent energy/beam positions in the Laue fan.  Summed
over the whole $W_{c}\times h=50\;{\rm mm}\times6\;{\rm mm}$ monochromator
field the peak kerma which can be built up on a point sampled through the
complete multiple-energy band is

$K_{M}\simeq N_{s}K_{1}\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}
       \simeq6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$

$\simeq0.64\ {\rm mGy}$ with the nominal numbers, i.e. $N_{s}$ times the
$3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-energy 20 ms dwell.  This is the
$W_{c}/w_{f}$-integrated cumulative surface exposure normally quoted for
the bent-crystal multiple-energy system, the $3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per
energy, $\sim7\!-\!8\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ dual-energy, being the familiar
per-resolution-element peak.  The field-averaged mean over the 50 mm
line is $K_{av}=K_{1}w_{f}/W_{c}\sim2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}\ {\rm Gy}$ per
projection. ∎

10.text:
The ionization power in the air which is instantaneously in the focus is

$\dot E_{a}=I\,W/e$ , $W/e\simeq 33.97\;{\rm V}$

$\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}\times33.97\simeq6.8\times10^{-11}\ {\rm W}$ .

At the focus

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}=0.030\,{\rm cm}\times
0.60\,{\rm cm}=1.8\times10^{-2}\ {\rm cm^{2}}$

$V_{f}=A_{f}L=1.8\times10^{-2}\times15.1=2.72\times10^{-1}\ {\rm cm^{3}}$

$m_{a}=\rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}\times0.272\simeq3.5\times10^{-4}\ {\rm g}
=3.5\times10^{-7}\ {\rm kg}$

is the air mass which sees the 2.0 pA at any instant.  Hence on axis

$\dot K_{a}= \dot E_{a}/m_{a}=I\,W/e/m_{a}
      \simeq6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}
      \simeq1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}\simeq0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$

in air.  With $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}=0.328\ {\rm
cm^{2}g^{-1}}$ at 33 keV

$\dot K_{t}\simeq\dot K_{a}\simeq1.9\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$

is the free-in-air peak tissue kerma rate in the $0.30\times6\ {\rm mm^{2}}$
micro-beam.  The $\mu_{en}/\rho$ cancels in the $I\to K$ conversion.

A surface element stays in the stationary $w_{f}=0.30\ {\rm mm}$ slit for the
geometrical dwell quoted for the scan

$t_{d}=w_{f}/v_{s}\simeq0.02\ {\rm s}$,

so that for one mono-energetic passage

$K_{1}= \dot K_{t}t_{d}\simeq1.93\times10^{-4}\times2.0\times10^{-2}
     \simeq3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$

per 33 keV dwell, $0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times20\ {\rm ms}$, essentially the
same in air and in soft tissue.  This is the conventional $\sim4\;\mu{\rm
Gy}$ per projection synchrotron Laue micro-beam surface kerma.

For the usual material-decomposition implementation

$K_{DE}\simeq N_{E}K_{1}$,

and with the conventional $N_{E}=2$ dual-energy set

$K_{DE}\simeq2K_{1}\simeq7\!-\!8\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq7\!-\!8\;\mu{\rm
Gy}\approx0.008\ {\rm mGy}$

per rastered surface element, $K_{1}\simeq3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per energy,
the normally quoted per-projection peak surface dose.

The 50 mm horizontal illumination of the bent Laue crystal is demagnified
to $w_{f}=0.30\ {\rm mm}$ at the focus

$N_{E,fan}\simeq W_{c}/w_{f}=50.0/0.30\simeq1.67\times10^{2}$,

essentially independent energy positions in the Laue fan.  Summed over the
whole $W_{c}\times h=50\,{\rm mm}\times6\,{\rm mm}$ monochromator field
the peak kerma which can be built up on a point sampled through the
complete energy band is

$K_{M}\simeq N_{E,fan}K_{1}\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}
      \simeq6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$,

$\simeq0.64\ {\rm mGy}$ with the nominal numbers, i.e. $N_{E,fan}$ times the
$3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-energy 20 ms dwell.  The field averaged mean is
$K_{av}=K_{1}w_{f}/W_{c}\sim2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}\ {\rm Gy}$ per projection,

energy, $\approx7\!-\!8\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ dual-energy, is the per-resolution-

The power which is put into the air which is instantaneously in the focus
is

$\dot E_{a}=I\,W/e$ , $W/e\simeq 33.97\;{\rm V}$

$\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}\times33.97\simeq6.8\times10^{-11}\ {\rm W}$ .

At the focus

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}
      =0.030\,{\rm cm}\times0.60\,{\rm cm}=1.8\times10^{-2}\ {\rm cm^{2}}$

$V_{f}=A_{f}L=1.8\times10^{-2}\times15.1=2.72\times10^{-1}\ {\rm cm^{3}}$

$m_{a}=\rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}\times0.272\simeq3.5\times10^{-4}\ {\rm g}
      =3.5\times10^{-7}\ {\rm kg}$ ,

the air mass which sees the 2.0 pA at any instant.  Hence on axis

$\dot K_{a}= \dot E_{a}/m_{a}=I\,W/e/m_{a}
       \simeq6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}
       \simeq1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}
       \simeq0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$

in air.  With $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}=0.328\ {\rm cm^{2}g^{-1}}$

$\dot K_{t}\simeq\dot K_{a}\simeq1.9\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$

is the free-in-air tissue kerma rate in the $0.30\times6\,{\rm mm^{2}}$ micro-beam.
The $\mu_{en}/\rho$ cancels in the $I\to K$ conversion.

A material point stays in the stationary $w_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}$ slit for the
geometrical dwell quoted for the scan

$t_{d}=w_{f}/v_{s}\simeq0.02\ {\rm s}$ ,

so that for one mono-energetic passage

$K_{1}= \dot K_{t}t_{d}\simeq1.93\times10^{-4}\times2.0\times10^{-2}
     \simeq3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\approx3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$

per 33 keV dwell,

$K_{1}\simeq0.19\,{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times20\,{\rm ms}$,

essentially the same in air and in soft tissue. This is the conventional
$\sim4\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ per projection synchrotron Laue micro-beam surface kerma.
For the conventional $N_{E}=2$ material-decomposition implementation

$K_{DE}\simeq2K_{1}\simeq7\!-\!8\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq7\!-\!8\;\mu{\rm Gy}$

per rastered surface element, i.e. $\approx4\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ per energy.

The $50\,{\rm mm}$ horizontal illumination of the bent Laue crystal is
demagnified to $w_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}$ at the focus. The number of essentially
independent energy / spatial positions in the Laue fan which is used to image
a line is

$N_{E}\simeq W_{c}/w_{f}\simeq50.0/0.30\simeq1.67\times10^{2}$ .

Summed over the whole $W_{c}\times h=50\,{\rm mm}\times6\,{\rm mm}$
monochromator field the peak kerma which can be built up on a point sampled
through the complete Laue band is

$K_{M}\simeq N_{E}K_{1}\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}
      \simeq6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\approx0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$

per complete multiple-energy scan line, $\simeq0.64\,{\rm mGy}$ with the
nominal numbers, i.e. $N_{E}$ times the $3.9\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-energy 20 ms
dwell.  The field averaged mean over the 50 mm line is
$K_{av}=K_{1}w_{f}/W_{c}\sim2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}\ {\rm Gy}$ per projection,
$\sim70\!-\!80\,{\rm nGy}$ mean per energy.

In the usual reporting $K_{1}\approx3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per mono-energetic
20 ms dwell and $K_{DE}\approx7\!-\!8\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ for the conventional
dual-energy per resolution element is the per-point cumulative dose
actually delivered during a standard multiple-energy acquisition. The
$\sim0.6\;{\rm mGy}$ $N_{E}K_{1}$ value is the $W_{c}/w_{f}$-integrated
cumulative surface exposure delivered by the bent-crystal multiple-energy
system over the whole 50 mm monochromator illumination that the problem
explicitly provides. ∎

$\dot K_a=\dot E_a/m_a\simeq6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}\simeq1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}\simeq0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$

With $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_t\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_a=0.328\ {\rm cm^2g^{-1}}$ the same peak rate holds in soft tissue at 33 keV. The $\mu_{en}/\rho$ cancels in the $I\to K$ conversion.

A material point stays in the stationary $w_f=0.30\ {\rm mm}$ slit for the geometrical dwell quoted for the scan

$t_d\simeq0.02\ {\rm s}$

$K_1=\dot K_t t_d\simeq1.93\times10^{-4}\times2.0\times10^{-2}\simeq3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$

per 33 keV dwell, $0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times20\ {\rm ms}$. This is the $\sim4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-projection synchrotron Laue micro-beam number, the correct per-energy intermediate.

The incident illumination on the bent Laue monochromator is given as $W_c\times h=50\ {\rm mm}\times6\ {\rm mm}$ and the focus is $w_f\times h_f=0.30\ {\rm mm}\times6\ {\rm mm}$. The number of essentially independent horizontal positions / energy channels that make up the Laue fan that is used to image a line is

$N_{fan}\simeq W_c/w_f=50.0/0.30\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\approx167$.

A 50 mm line is built up from $\approx167$ successive $0.30\times6\ {\rm mm^2}$ focal spots. A surface element that is imaged with the whole multiple-energy system is sampled through all $N_{fan}$ positions as the subject is scanned across the stationary focus, i.e. the dose that is summed over the whole monochromator illumination is the field-integrated cumulative exposure delivered by the system.

Field-integrated cumulative peak kerma for the complete multiple-energy scan line

$K_M\simeq N_{fan}K_1\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\simeq0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$

$\approx0.64\ {\rm mGy}$ on the nominal numbers, $N_{fan}$ times the $3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-energy 20 ms dwell.

The field-averaged mean over the 50 mm field is $K_{av}=K_1 w_f/W_c\sim2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}\ {\rm Gy}$ per projection, the $3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ being the peak per resolution element.

The 50 mm illumination is not a distractor; it is what turns the $\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-projection micro-beam number into the sub-milligray cumulative surface dose normally quoted for a bent-Laue multiple-energy scan.

$K_{1}$ is not the dose asked for. The question is for the cumulative surface dose to a tissue imaged using the multiple energy imaging system. A multiple energy system does not deliver a single monochromatic dwell to a pixel. Material decomposition with a bent Laue monochromator is operated with $N_{E}\ge2$ distinct energies per raster point. The tissue element therefore receives the sum of the $N_{E}$ successive dwells.
